summary: Nigel Allan works in history, archaeology, and other fields. Attested in 1993, he served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust, where he succeeded Marianne Winder.

Niharranjan Ray (1903–1981) worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1924–1926) and completed a doctoral dissertation at Leiden University (~1935–1936), later working at Calcutta (~1937–1965) and directing IIAS (~1965–1970).

Nika Jovic specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Géza Bethlenfalvy (2007–2008) and earned her Magistra der Philosophie under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes at the University of Vienna (attested 2010).

Nikolai Solmsdorf is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at LMU Munich (attested 2013) under supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard, Jens-Uwe Hartmann, and Alexander von Rospatt, and held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).

Nina Mirnig is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who founded the University of Oxford in 2008 and completed her DPhil there under Alexis Sanderson in 2010. By 2020, she was affiliated with the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Ninian Smart (1927–2001) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher educated at Oxford and Yale. He taught at Nottingham (~1960–1961), Birmingham (~1961–1967), and Lancaster University (1967), and later served as J. F. Rowny Professor at UC Santa Barbara (attested 1993–2001).

Nirajan Kafle is an Indology scholar who studied under Diwakar Acharya, Bhim Kandel, and Kashinath Nyupane, completing a doctorate at Leiden under Peter Bisschop by 2015. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2019) and Leiden (attested 2021).

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti (1893–1956) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Cambridge, Paris, and Berlin. He taught at the University of Calcutta (1917) and held multiple roles at the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as Director General from 1948 to 1950.

Nirmal Chandra Sinha (1911–1997) worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Calcutta and Presidency University, later serving at Krishnath College, the National Archives of India (~1944–1958), and the University of Calcutta as Centenary Professor of International Relations.
Nirupam Chakma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015) under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.
Noa Gal is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Shlomo Biderman and earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (Wolfson College) under Richard Gombrich by 2003, later serving as a Visiting Research Fellow at Stanford University.

Noboru Karashima (1933–2015) was a historian and Indologist educated at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1962). He held teaching posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1964–1967), the University of Tokyo (~1974–1994), Taisho University (~1994–2009), and the Open University of Japan.
Noboru Ueda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and served as a professor at Mejiro University (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani (born 1944) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at Otani University and Kyoto University. He taught at Otani University Junior College (~1978–1984; president ~2002–2007) and served as professor at Otani University (~1984–2015).

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara (attested 1962). He held assistant professorships at the University of Toronto (attested 1969) and Kyoto University (attested 1979).

Nobuhiro Ota (born 1969) is an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1988–1998). He served as a Research Fellow at the University of Tokyo (~1998–2000) and held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2008).
Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a research student at Taisho University and served as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpoin (attested 2014).

Tensho Miyazaki (born 1978) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2005–2008). He held posts at Toyo University (~2008–2011), the University of Tokyo (~2012–2016), and Tokyo University of Agriculture (attested 2015).

Nobumi Iyanaga (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held a lecturing post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003) and conducted research on contract at the Tokyo Centre of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2008–2014).
